title: Christina Caron identifies teens after Urban Air kindness
excerpt: Christina Caron used Facebook to identify the teenagers who played with her 7-year-old son Tristan at Urban Air in Bellingham. Urban Air said it plans to invite everyone involved back for a special day.
body:
Christina Caron used Facebook to identify the teenagers who played with her 7-year-old son Tristan at Urban Air Adventure Park in Bellingham, Massachusetts, after the group spent about 40 minutes including him in their games. Urban Air management also said it planned to invite everyone involved back for a special day, according to WTN Global.

The encounter happened at the indoor adventure park when Christina Caron was there with Tristan, who has autism. A group of teenagers noticed him sitting alone and invited him to join them. According to Sunny Skyz, the interaction began when Livy Molinari commented on a ball Tristan had won and asked if she could hold it for a moment.

That simple exchange turned into a longer play session. Sunny Skyz reported that the teens and Tristan spent about 40 minutes together, playing catch, hide-and-seek and using the slides. Hoodline later reported that the group included Molinari, Anna Hele, Kelsey Zozzaro and Kenny Leite, though the exact day of the visit was not established in the reporting reviewed.

The teenagers later said they did not know Tristan had autism when they invited him to play. Sunny Skyz, citing WBZ-TV, reported that Anna Hele said, “We just wanted to include him and have a fun time playing around at Urban Air.” The same report said Kenny Leite added, “It's nice we included him and other people get to know about this, so maybe they can think about it when other people aren't included.”

Christina Caron said the gesture meant a great deal because her son is not always treated with kindness. Sunny Skyz reported that she said, “More often than not, he's not met with kindness,” and later added, “A small act of kindness can really turn someone's day around. It can change the trajectory, and it just meant so much to me.”

Hoodline reported that Caron used Facebook to find the teenagers and thank them personally. The same report said Urban Air had reached out and planned to invite the group back. Hoodline also noted that the Bellingham park runs a monthly Sensory Friendly Play session on the second Sunday of each month.

WTN Global reported that Urban Air owner Chad Darling said the facility has operated for about eight years, making it a frequent backdrop for children making new friends.

title: Rubio says Ukraine hit ships tied to U.S. oil interests
excerpt: Marco Rubio said Ukraine struck ships or oil supplies linked to American interests and denied that U.S. intelligence-sharing for Ukraine had been paused.
body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday in Uzbekistan that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing for Ukraine used to warn Kyiv about Russian ballistic missile attacks, while also repeating a claim that Ukrainian strikes hit ships or oil supplies tied to American interests in the Black Sea. His comments came a day after a Breitbart interview in which he said American companies had complained that oil on a ship hit by Ukraine belonged to them.

“There’s been no pause. Zelensky should be focused on bringing an end to this war,” Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan, according to the New York Post’s account of his remarks.

In the same report, Rubio said, “We have seen strikes on energy vessels in the Black Sea. And there’s been complaints, a lot, because we have American companies calling us and saying, ‘Hey, that was our oil on that ship that was hit by Ukraine.’” He added that he did not believe Ukraine intentionally targeted the vessels.

Rubio had already made a similar allegation on Sept. 22 in an interview with Fox News. ABC News reported that he said “the one thing we are concerned about” was that over the previous few months, “American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine.” ABC said it was not immediately clear what specific incidents Rubio meant.

The Kyiv Post likewise reported on Sept. 22 that Rubio did not publicly name the vessels or clarify whether they were American-owned, U.S.-flagged or connected to the United States through cargo, chartering or energy infrastructure. The outlet wrote that the claim appeared to refer to vessels using Russia’s Black Sea ports to transport oil connected to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which carries Kazakh crude. Kyiv Post reported that no public evidence had established that U.S.-owned or U.S.-flagged ships were repeatedly hit.

ABC News separately reported that the Caspian Pipeline Consortium counts American oil giants Chevron and ExxonMobil among its top shareholders. Rubio also said the United States supported the idea of an energy infrastructure ceasefire in which neither Ukraine’s infrastructure nor Russian energy supplies would be targeted. ABC quoted him as saying, “We think that would be a great idea, an energy infrastructure of cease fire, in which you're not- Ukraine's infrastructure is not being targeted. Russian energy supplies are not being targeted as well. It's an ideal outcome.”

The comments surfaced amid a tense stretch in U.S.-Ukraine relations. The New York Post reported that tensions rose after President Trump’s Oct. 9 announcement that the United States would import hundreds of thousands of gallons of diesel fuel, and after Trump halted plans on Friday to implement sanctions on Moscow under a bipartisan bill.

Rubio’s remarks also collided with a public dispute over intelligence sharing. On NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, “But only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it.” The New York Post reported that Rubio responded Monday by rejecting the suggestion that Washington had paused that specific sharing.

The exact ships or cargoes Rubio was referring to were not identified in the supplied reporting. What the available accounts do show is that Rubio is continuing to press the argument that Ukraine should avoid strikes that affect energy shipping and supplies with American links, even as Washington and Kyiv dispute how U.S. intelligence and wartime targeting are being handled.

sources.title: Rubio says Ukraine unintentionally hit 'American-linked' oil infrastructure
key_facts: Secretary of State Marco Rubio alleged that U.S.-linked oil infrastructure has been targeted in recent weeks by Ukraine amid its war with Russia during an interview with Fox News on Tuesday morning, though he conceded it was "probably not" deliberate.

Rubio, who attributed the recent rise in oil prices to conflict in the Black Sea between Russia and Ukraine as well as in Yemen with the Houthis, said in the interview that one of the U.S.'s concerns amid Russia's war was being unintentionally caught in the crosshairs.

"The one thing we are concerned about, however, is that over the last few months, on a number of occasions, American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine.
It was not immediately clear what specific incidents Rubio was referencing, though Ukraine has conducted strikes on the Russian Black Sea port Novorossiysk.
Rubio told Fox News that the U.S. was enthusiastic about the concept of an energy infrastructure ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, something Zelenskyy also called for on Monday.

key_facts: Public reporting confirms that Washington previously asked Kyiv to avoid attacks on non-Russian tankers and infrastructure connected to US energy companies, but does not show that US-flagged or US-owned ships were repeatedly hit.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News on Tuesday,  Sept. 22, that Ukraine had repeatedly targeted vessels linked to the United States in recent months, probably unintentionally.

According to the report, Ukraine agreed not to target CPC infrastructure or non-Russian vessels as long as those ships were not under Ukrainian sanctions and were not carrying Russian oil or other Russian cargo.
No publicly available report has established that Ukraine repeatedly struck ships sailing under the US flag or owned by US companies.
Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian-linked shipping and oil infrastructure in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov in 2026.

key_facts: Marco Rubio says Ukrainian strikes have created a problem Washington cannot ignore.

Speaking to Fox News on Tuesday, Rubio accused Ukraine of striking vessels linked to the United States and supplies ultimately destined for the US – even while acknowledging that Kyiv may not have intended to hit them.

Fox News separately described Rubio’s remarks as concerning “American-linked ships and oil supplies.”
Rubio said several incidents involving ships with US connections had occurred during recent months.

issues.claim: "Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday in Uzbekistan that the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing for Ukraine ... while also repeating a claim that Ukrainian strikes hit ships or oil supplies tied to American interests in the Black Sea."
issues.problem: This lead sentence conflates two different settings. The sources say Rubio denied any intelligence-sharing pause on Monday in Uzbekistan, but his renewed claim about ships/oil tied to American interests came in a Breitbart interview released Sunday, not in the Uzbekistan remarks.
issues.fix: Separate the developments by venue and timing: e.g., "On Monday in Uzbekistan, Rubio said the Trump administration had not paused intelligence-sharing for Ukraine. In a Breitbart interview released Sunday, he separately repeated his claim that Ukrainian strikes had hit ships or cargoes tied to American oil interests in the Black Sea."

fact_check.summary: One chronology/venue issue: the lead blurs Rubio's Monday Uzbekistan comments with a separate claim he made in a Breitbart interview released the day before.
